summary:
Northern Ireland carries three sub-national negatives absent elsewhere in the UK: Education Minister Paul Givan ordered the 2019 transgender-pupils guidance withdrawn from the Education Authority website in September 2025 after the FWS ruling, calling it "unlawful and flawed" and a product of "activist campaigns"; the Justice Minister's attempt to include transgender people as a protected group in hate-crime sentencing reform was stalled (reported DUP obstruction); and the Rainbow Project records a pattern of paramilitary-flavoured anti-LGB&T violence including a pipe bomb thrown through the home of a trans woman in Derry/Londonderry described by PSNI as a "sectarian hate crime," a 2019 Belfast city-centre assault hospitalising a gay man, and an average of ~290 anti-LGB&T incidents per year (2013–2017) with rising transgender-identity strand counts to September 2025.

Counter-balancing: PSNI/NISRA track a separate "transgender identity" category (unlike England and Wales), evidencing institutional recognition; the Health Minister publicly defended gender-identity service funding (£800k+ uplift) against DUP/TUV criticism, showing the executive is split rather than uniformly hostile. No criminal ban on expression or police-enforced facility prohibition exists — the risk mechanism mirrors the national EHRC code (service refusal by staff) plus street-level violence.

sources.summary: BBC News NI (8 September 2025): the Education Authority's 2019 guidance on supporting transgender pupils is withdrawn from its website after the UK Supreme Court biological-sex ruling; Education Minister Paul Givan requested the withdrawal, said the guidance did not reflect departmental policy and was inconsistent with NI law, and called it a product of activist campaigns; opposition parties press for reinstatement and disclosure of the legal advice.

BBC: the Justice Minister's attempt to add transgender people as a protected group in Northern Ireland's hate-crime sentencing reform is being stalled, with the DUP reported to be blocking the measure.

Daily Mirror: an exploding pipe bomb was thrown through the window of the home of Rachael Keys, a 27-year-old trans woman, in the Lincoln Court area of Derry/Londonderry while she watched television; PSNI treated it as a hate crime with sectarian framing and she was forced to move out.

Rainbow Project Northern Ireland hate-crime monitoring page: an average of about 290 reported anti-LGB&T incidents and crimes per year (2013–2017), reporting stagnant, and quarterly series running back to 2004/05 including a separate transgender-identity strand.
BBC: the Health Minister publicly defends an uplift of more than £800k for gender-identity health services against DUP/TUV criticism, evidencing a divided executive rather than uniform hostility.

tangentialFactors: The violence record mixes anti-gay and anti-trans incidents (the 2019 Belfast assault was anti-gay; the ~290/year series counts anti-LGB&T broadly) — the trans strand is smaller but separately tracked and rising.
localsOnly: The withdrawn school guidance bore on trans pupils in resident families; the stalled protected-group reform concerns sentencing for offences against residents — a visitor encounters both as climate and policing-culture signals rather than direct machinery.
